Slander is described as a gross lie and hideous fabrication. A report adds that harming believers despite their good conduct is even worse. Allah protects the wronged believer and is angered on their behalf.

phrases.translation: O Prophet! Ask your wives, daughters, and believing women to draw their cloaks over their bodies.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet's wives, daughters, and believing women are told to draw outer garments around themselves when going out for a need. Reports describe covering the head and face with one eye visible, or wrapping and fastening the garment at the forehead. The common purpose is modest coverage that distinguished free women from the dress associated with slave-women.

phrases.translation: In this way it is more likely that they will be recognized ˹as virtuous˺ and not be harassed.
phrases.explanation: This coverage made it more likely that passersby would recognize them as free women and that immoral harassers would refrain from hurtful words or suspicious remarks. Reports describe men harassing women along the road at night. The verse states the intended protective effect of the dress rule while identifying the harassers' own words and conduct as reprehensible.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Allah is forgiving concerning earlier negligence in drawing the outer garments properly and merciful in not punishing women after they repent and observe the instruction. The closing names place the command within an opportunity for correction. Previous failure is not presented as beyond pardon when followed by sincere return and changed conduct.

phrases.translation: If the hypocrites, and those with sickness in their hearts, and rumour-mongers in Medina do not desist,
phrases.explanation: The warning addresses hypocrites who conceal unbelief while displaying faith, people whose diseased hearts are explained through lust and pursuit of fornication, and rumor-mongers spreading false reports in Medina. Their rumors included claims of approaching armies and reports against the Prophet and believers. All three are commanded to stop their distinct but socially damaging conduct.

phrases.translation: We will certainly incite you ˹O Prophet˺ against them,
phrases.explanation: If they persist, Allah promises to give the Prophet power over them and incite him against them. The threat follows their refusal to desist, not mere suspicion about hidden thoughts. Divine enablement would turn their apparent position within Medina into vulnerability, ending the security from which they spread hypocrisy, immorality, and falsehood.

phrases.translation: and then they will not be your neighbours there any longer
phrases.explanation: Afterward they would remain near the Prophet in Medina for only a short time before being banished and driven out. Their neighborhood with him would end rather than continue indefinitely. The warning reportedly led some to suppress what they had intended to reveal of their hypocrisy, showing that the announced consequence demanded an immediate change in conduct.

phrases.translation: ˹They deserve to be˺ condemned.
phrases.explanation: The persistent opponents are described as accursed, driven away, and banished. This continues the warning directed at those who refuse to abandon hypocrisy and harmful rumor. Their condemnation is not a social insult invented by the believers but a stated divine consequence for openly persisting in the conduct just described.

phrases.translation: ˹If they were to persist,˺ they would get themselves seized and killed relentlessly wherever they are found
phrases.explanation: If they openly display their hypocrisy and persist, the verse warns that they will be seized and killed wherever encountered because of their unbelief. The commentary explicitly connects the killing with public manifestation of hypocrisy. The statement therefore belongs to the threatened confrontation in this passage, not to hidden doubts or mere membership in a group.

phrases.translation: That was Allah’s way with those ˹hypocrites˺ who have gone before.
phrases.explanation: This treatment was Allah's established way with earlier people of the same kind who made their hypocrisy public. The commentary describes the consequence as thorough killing and abundant curse when concealed opposition became open. The present warning is thus placed within a recurring divine pattern of dealing with manifested hypocrisy, not presented as an unprecedented reaction.

phrases.translation: And you will find no change in Allah’s way
phrases.explanation: The Prophet will find no alteration in the way Allah has instituted among His creatures. He can therefore be certain that Allah will not change that pattern concerning these hypocrites. The statement grounds confidence in the warning: the announced consequence does not depend on changing public strength or on the opponents' apparent security within Medina.

phrases.translation: People ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the Hour. Say, “That knowledge is only with Allah.
phrases.explanation: When people ask the Prophet when the Hour will come, he must tell them that its timing is known only to Allah. No one else possesses that knowledge. Prophetic office does not make the unseen schedule of resurrection available for human disclosure, so the question is answered by directing them to the limits of created knowledge.

phrases.translation: You never know, perhaps the Hour is near.”
phrases.explanation: The Hour may be near. Indeed, the commentary says its appointed coming has drawn near and its moment approached. The answer therefore replaces curiosity about an exact date with awareness of possible nearness. Not knowing the time does not justify assuming a distant future or becoming indifferent to its arrival.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah condemns the disbelievers, and has prepared for them a blazing Fire
phrases.explanation: Allah has cursed those who disbelieve in Him, removing them from all good and keeping them far from it. He has also prepared a blazing Fire for them in the Hereafter, ignited to burn them. The warning about the Hour therefore moves immediately to the consequence awaiting persistent disbelief when that appointed reality arrives.

phrases.translation: to stay there for ever and ever—never will they find any protector or helper
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers will remain in the blazing Fire eternally, without end. No protector will take charge of them and rescue them from it, and no helper will deliver them from the punishment Allah imposes. Their complete isolation from effective aid reinforces that no created power can reverse the judgment or provide an escape after it.

phrases.translation: On the Day their faces are ˹constantly˺ flipped in the Fire,
phrases.explanation: On that Day, the disbelievers' faces will be turned over repeatedly in the Fire, one state after another, with no protector or helper. The image emphasizes ongoing punishment rather than a single passing moment. It follows the declaration that they remain there eternally and makes their utter helplessness physically visible.

phrases.translation: they will cry, “Oh! If only we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!”
phrases.explanation: In that condition they will wish they had obeyed Allah and His Messenger during worldly life, following the commands and prohibitions he brought. The commentary says such obedience would have placed them with the people of Paradise. Their cry expresses immense regret, but it comes after the opportunity for the obedience they now recognize has passed.

phrases.translation: And they will say, “Our Lord! We obeyed our leaders and elite, but they led us astray from the ˹Right˺ Way
phrases.explanation: In Hell, the disbelievers will confess that they obeyed their leaders and prominent figures in error and idolatry. Those leaders caused them to leave the path of truth and guidance: belief in Allah, acknowledgment of His oneness, and sincere obedience to Him. Their statement identifies the human influence through which they abandoned the right way.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! Give them double ˹our˺ punishment,
phrases.explanation: They will ask Allah to give those leaders double the punishment that they themselves receive. The request follows their confession that obedience to those figures led them astray. It expresses their recognition of the leaders' role in guiding them into idolatry and error, now that the consequences of following them are unavoidable.

phrases.translation: and condemn them tremendously.”
phrases.explanation: They will also ask Allah to curse those leaders with a tremendous curse, explained as humiliating them greatly. Their plea turns against the authorities they once obeyed. The closing scene therefore exposes the collapse of loyalty to misguiding leaders when both leaders and followers face divine judgment.

phrases.translation: O believers! Do not be like those who slandered Moses,
phrases.explanation: Believers must not hurt Allah's Messenger through speech or deeds displeasing to him, as people hurt Moses through false accusations and slander. The instruction addresses conduct toward Muhammad by comparison with an earlier prophet. Harm is broader than verbal abuse alone and includes actions the Messenger would not love.

phrases.translation: but Allah cleared him of what they said.
phrases.explanation: Allah cleared Moses by exposing the falsehood of what was said. Reports describe accusations of bodily defects, followed by the incident of his garment and the moving rock, or an accusation that he killed Aaron, followed by angelic clarification of Aaron's death. The commentary allows all these reports rather than selecting only one.

phrases.translation: And he was honourable in the sight of Allah
phrases.explanation: Moses held high standing with Allah: he was honored, accepted, and one whose intercession was answered because of his obedience. This divine rank contrasts with the slanders directed at him. Human accusations did not diminish his position before Allah, and the clearing of his name demonstrated the honor he already possessed.

phrases.translation: O believers! Be mindful of Allah,
phrases.explanation: Believers must fear Allah by refusing to disobey Him, lest they deserve His punishment. Mindfulness is therefore active restraint under divine authority, not merely an emotion. This command prepares for the truthful speech that follows and places both words and conduct under the same duty of obedience.

phrases.translation: and say what is right
phrases.explanation: They must speak words that are upright, accurate, true, and just, especially concerning Allah's Messenger and fellow believers, rather than improper or false words. Reports extend uprightness to all conduct and also identify the declaration that there is no god but Allah. Speech should therefore be fitting in content and grounded in truth.

phrases.translation: He will bless your deeds for you,
phrases.explanation: Through mindfulness and right speech, Allah makes believers fit for good deeds and sets their works right. The promise concerns moral repair and successful righteous action, not merely public approval of what they already do. Divine help transforms their conduct after they respond to the command.

phrases.translation: and forgive your sins.
phrases.explanation: Allah will also pardon their sins and not punish them for them. This joins correction of future action with forgiveness of past failure. The believer is not asked to repair conduct while carrying an unalterable burden of former sin. Divine pardon accompanies the promised setting right of deeds.

phrases.translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, has truly achieved a great triumph
phrases.explanation: Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger by doing what is commanded, avoiding what is forbidden, and speaking rightly achieves a great triumph. The commentary calls it the greatest honor from Allah. True success is therefore defined by obedient faith and its divine reward, not by status among the misguiding leaders described earlier.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains,
phrases.explanation: The trust includes Allah's obedience, religious obligations, and prescribed duties, but the commentary's preferred meaning encompasses every kind of trust, including trusts between people. The offer involved responsibility with reward for fulfillment and punishment for neglect. It therefore concerns accountable fidelity rather than an unnamed object with no moral obligations attached.

phrases.translation: but they ˹all˺ declined to bear it, being fearful of it.
phrases.explanation: The heavens, earth, and mountains refused to bear this responsibility and feared falling short in its duties. One report explains that their refusal was reverence for Allah's religion, not disobedience, and that they preferred remaining subservient to His command without reward and punishment. Their fear highlighted the gravity of accountable trust.

phrases.translation: But humanity assumed it,
phrases.explanation: Humanity, represented in reports by Adam, accepted the trust with its consequences: reward for doing well and punishment for doing wrong. Unlike the refusal described before, the human being undertook accountable responsibility. The wider interpretation also includes fulfillment or betrayal of religious duties, promises, speech, and property entrusted by other people.

phrases.translation: ˹for˺ they are truly wrongful ˹to themselves˺ and ignorant ˹of the consequences˺
phrases.explanation: The human being is described as wronging himself or the trust and being ignorant of its right, consequences, or true benefit. Reports apply the description to Adam's acceptance and failure, while another narrative applies it to Cain's betrayal of a family trust. Across these reports, the central failure is accepting responsibility without faithfully fulfilling its right.

phrases.translation: so that Allah will punish hypocrite men and women and polytheistic men and women,
phrases.explanation: The trust distinguishes those who betray it from those who fulfill it. Hypocrite men and women outwardly claim to meet Allah's obligations while concealing disbelief. Polytheistic men and women worship gods and idols alongside Allah. Punishment is connected with these betrayals, and women as well as men are explicitly addressed in the outcome.

phrases.translation: and Allah will turn in mercy to believing men and women.
phrases.explanation: Allah turns in mercy to believing men and women by bringing them back to His obedience and enabling them to fulfill the trusts He imposed until they complete them. Their fulfillment is itself supported by divine mercy. The contrast is not simply between labels but between betrayal of responsibility and restored, faithful performance of it.

phrases.translation: For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Allah forgives the sins of believing men and women, covering those sins and withholding punishment after their repentance. His mercy completes the chapter's closing contrast. Even those who fulfill the trust remain dependent on pardon for shortcomings, while hypocrisy and idolatry require a return to sincere faith and obedience.
